summary: Bumps the exact @cipherstash/protect-ffi pin 0.30.0 -> 0.31.0 for @cipherstash/stack (runtime dependency) and two adapters (devDependency) and adapts to its breaking changes: ProtectError class replaced by an isProtectErrorCode value check (native getErrorCode and DynamoDB handleError), WASM newClient options reshaped (authStrategy + clientOpts, no cast_as pre-normalisation), and the undeclared correlation `id` stripped from bulk/model payloads. The upgrade also makes an explicitly supplied clientKey hex-only, a deliberate breaking change carried as a `major` changeset, documented in the shipped stash-auth skill and guarded in CI by a new hex pre-flight. I checked that every native bulk/model call site now strips `id` while keeping positional correlation and lockContext, and that the WASM batch paths already built explicit payloads. The main residual risks are (1) customers with base64 keys failing at construction on upgrade, which is intentional and documented but is a runtime outage for them, and (2) the native entry still passing the OIDC/auth strategy under the old `strategy` key, which 0.31 renamed to `authStrategy`; nothing in CI exercises that path against the real 0.31 binding because the identity suites skip without USER_JWT. Error-code reclassification is intended and unit-tested. All 16 CI checks passed on head.

behaviour_changes.description: @cipherstash/stack's exact runtime pin on @cipherstash/protect-ffi moves 0.30.0 -> 0.31.0 (all six per-platform native binaries change); stack-drizzle and stack-supabase devDependency pins move with it. Upgrading stack forces the new FFI.

An explicitly supplied clientKey (config.clientKey or CS_CLIENT_KEY) must now be hex; base64 values that previously worked are rejected at client construction with a deliberately terse message. Change comes from protect-ffi 0.31; stack ships it as a major release.

Error codes surfaced to callers are now only those accepted by protect-ffi's isProtectErrorCode. Native operations: getErrorCode reads `code` structurally instead of `instanceof ProtectError`. DynamoDB handleError: foreign string codes (e.g. ECONNRESET) are no longer passed through and become DYNAMODB_ENCRYPTION_ERROR.

The WASM entry calls newClient with `authStrategy` and `clientOpts: { clientId, clientKey }` instead of top-level `strategy`/`clientId`/`clientKey`, drops the `as never` cast, and passes encryptConfig with SDK cast_as spellings ('string', 'number', ...) unnormalised, relying on 0.31 to normalise in Rust.

Bulk encrypt/decrypt and all model encrypt/decrypt paths (with and without lock context) no longer forward the stack-side correlation `id` to protect-ffi; results are still mapped back to keys by array index.
The shared require-cs-secrets CI action gains a step that fails every credentialed job unless CS_CLIENT_KEY is even-length hex; the key is never echoed, only its length.
The customer-shipped stash-auth skill gains a warning that CS_CLIENT_KEY must be hex and how to recover on each entry point; a `stash` patch changeset is added for it.

failure_scenarios.title: Deployments with a base64 clientKey fail every operation after upgrading stack
failure_scenarios.trigger: A customer upgrades @cipherstash/stack to the new major while CS_CLIENT_KEY or config.clientKey holds the base64 key (e.g. copied from ~/.cipherstash/secretkey.json), which 0.30 accepted.
failure_scenarios.mechanism: protect-ffi 0.31 decodes an explicit clientKey as hex only (changeset and CI-action comment); stack pins protect-ffi exactly, so there is no opt-out. The error message is intentionally terse and does not mention base64.
failure_scenarios.consequence: Client construction fails and every encryption/decryption in that deployment fails until the key is re-encoded. Loud, fails closed, no data corruption, but a full outage of encrypted reads/writes for affected services. On wasm-inline there is no profile-store fallback.

existing_verification.description: require-cs-secrets hex pre-flight passed in every credentialed CI job, proving the repo's own CI key is hex and that the stack works with a hex key under 0.31

missing_verification: No test asserts the base64 rejection or its message on either entry (the behaviour lives in protect-ffi, which was not available to inspect).
No data on how many customers set base64 keys.
failure_scenarios.mitigation: Already mitigated by the major version bump, changeset and stash-auth skill text. Make the 2.0.0 release notes lead with this item, and consider a stack-side pre-check that recognises a base64-shaped key and names the encoding in the error (without echoing key material).

failure_scenarios.title: Native entry passes authStrategy under the pre-0.31 `strategy` key
failure_scenarios.trigger: A native-entry customer supplies config.authStrategy (e.g. OidcFederationStrategy for identity-bound lock context) and protect-ffi 0.31's native NewClientOptions does not honour `strategy`, or rejects it as an unknown key.
failure_scenarios.mechanism: This change renames the field to `authStrategy` for the WASM newClient (wasm-inline.ts:1554) because 0.31 renamed it and "both entries now deserialize the same NewClientOptions", but encryption/index.ts:143 still sends `strategy: config.authStrategy`. The only evidence that `strategy` still works is a test comment calling it a deprecated alias on the WASM side. Stack src is not typechecked in CI, so a removed field would not be caught at compile time either.
failure_scenarios.consequence: If the alias is rejected: every OIDC/identity-bound native client fails at construction. If it is silently ignored: the client falls back to CS_* credential auth, so operations run as the service rather than the end user, and identity-bound lock-context calls fail or lose their per-user authorisation.

failure_scenarios.mitigation: Pass `authStrategy: config.authStrategy` on the native newClient call, matching the WASM entry, and update init-strategy.test.ts. Or confirm the alias against the 0.31 source and record that in a comment.

failure_scenarios.title: Callers branching on error.code see different values
failure_scenarios.trigger: Application code branches on EncryptionError.code / EncryptedDynamoDBError.code, e.g. retrying on ECONNRESET from DynamoDB, or matching an FFI code that 0.31's isProtectErrorCode set does not include.
failure_scenarios.mechanism: handleError now replaces any code not accepted by isProtectErrorCode with DYNAMODB_ENCRYPTION_ERROR (dynamodb/helpers.ts:55-58). getErrorCode returns undefined for unrecognised codes (error-code.ts:20-21).
failure_scenarios.consequence: Retry or transport-error handling keyed on Node/AWS codes silently stops matching for DynamoDB operations. Any FFI code missing from the guard's set is flattened. Behavioural, recoverable, no data effect.

missing_verification: No check that every code the 0.31 binding actually throws is accepted by isProtectErrorCode (only UNKNOWN_COLUMN and INVALID_JSON_PATH are asserted).
failure_scenarios.mitigation: Documented in the major changeset. Reviewers should confirm the code list stack exposes in its types matches 0.31's PROTECT_ERROR_CODES.

WASM cast_as normalisation now depends on 0.31's Rust-side normalisation; the Deno E2E covers TextSearch/TextEq/IntegerOrd/Json only, so bigint, date, timestamp and boolean columns are not exercised on the WASM entry.

evidence.claim: @cipherstash/protect-ffi dependency pinned exactly to 0.31.0.
Collector reports protect-ffi 0.30.0 -> 0.31.0 in stack (dependencies) and stack-drizzle/stack-supabase (devDependencies).
Major changeset: clientKey must now be hex (base64 previously worked); DynamoDB foreign error codes no longer surfaced; WASM option shape and id stripping.
PR lists four breaking changes in 0.31 including credential move to clientOpts and strategy -> authStrategy rename, and says the live error-codes suite was not run locally.
Comment states 0.31 decodes explicit clientKey as hex only and rejects base64 with 'invalid clientKey: expected a hex-encoded key'.
getErrorCode reads error.code structurally and returns it only if isProtectErrorCode accepts it.
handleError maps any code not accepted by isProtectErrorCode to DYNAMODB_ENCRYPTION_ERROR.
WASM newClient now called with authStrategy, unnormalised encryptConfig, clientOpts { clientId, clientKey }, eqlVersion 3, no type cast.
Mocked unit tests assert the new clientOpts nesting and that cast_as 'string' is forwarded unnormalised.
withoutId strips id via map (order-preserving); single and multi model handlers correlate results by array index via keyMap.
createDecryptPayloads no longer forwards id; lockContext still spread in.
Lock-context model encrypt keeps lockContext on each item after id is stripped.
New step fails unless CS_CLIENT_KEY is an even-length hex string, printing only its length.
Shipped skill now warns that CS_CLIENT_KEY must be hex and gives per-entry recovery.
`stash env` converts the ZeroKMS base64 client key to hex, so keys minted this way are unaffected; base64 keys come from other sources such as secretkey.json.
Native newClient still receives the auth strategy under top-level `strategy`, with credentials and keyset in clientOpts.
All 16 check runs on head succeeded, including Run Tests (Node 22/24), Run E2E Tests, Run WASM E2E Tests (Deno) and the drizzle/supabase/prisma-next integration jobs.
Strategy forwarding is tested against a vi.mock of protect-ffi and asserts opts.strategy, so it cannot see the real 0.31 option schema.
Live OIDC/lock-context tests skip when USER_JWT is absent.
Only stated evidence that `strategy` is still accepted is a comment calling it a deprecated alias on the WASM newClient.
The run-tests job writes CS_* and DATABASE_URL to .env but no USER_JWT, so identity-bound live tests skip in CI.
New handleError tests cover foreign codes, a real FFI code, non-string codes and the throwPreservingCode round trip.
Deno WASM E2E schemas use only TextSearch, TextEq, IntegerOrd and Json domains (across roundtrip and query-types tests).
